# Application Index Audit and Deprecations

Use this skill when the target index has access, security, or forward-compatibility concerns:

- Access-denied errors are occurring on the index — users or services cannot read or write it
- Unexpected administrative actions were taken on the index (mapping changes, setting updates, alias modifications, deletion)
- Deprecation warnings are being logged against this index — signals breaking changes before a major upgrade
- Suspicious `run_as` or anonymous access (`user.name: _anonymous`) against the index

Note: Audit logging is active on this cluster. Absence of audit events for an index is itself meaningful — it means no access is occurring, which may indicate the index is disconnected from its expected consumers.

## Workflow

1. Use `app-index-triage-index_audit_access_denied` to identify users and source IPs repeatedly denied access — grouped by time bucket so spikes are visible.
2. Use `app-index-triage-index_admin_actions` to surface sensitive admin events (create/delete/put_mapping/update_settings/alias changes) and who performed them.
3. Use `app-index-triage-index_deprecation_warnings` to find deprecation keys for this index — each key corresponds to a specific deprecated feature that must be addressed before upgrading.

## Output guidance

- For access-denied: identify the user name, role, and source IP. Determine if it is a service account (expected pattern) or an anomalous user.
- For admin actions: note the timestamp, action type, and performing user. Flag any `delete_index` or `put_mapping` that was unexpected.
- For deprecation: summarize the deprecation key and recommend the remediation (consult Elasticsearch Deprecation API output or migration guide).
- Cross-reference access-denied spikes with the time of any admin action that may have changed index permissions.
description: Investigate access-denied audit events, sensitive admin actions, and deprecation warnings for the target index.
name: Application Index Audit and Deprecations
